name: Pramlintide
route: Injection under the skin immediately before major meals
status: FDA-approved (2005) as an add-on to mealtime insulin in adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes; boxed warning for severe hypoglycemia
mechanism: Stable copy of amylin, a hormone released with insulin, that slows stomach emptying, curbs glucagon after meals and increases fullness

article.summary: Pramlintide (SymlinPen) is an injectable copy of the hormone amylin, approved since 2005 as an add-on to mealtime insulin to smooth post-meal blood sugar in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
article.takeaway: Amylin is a hormone made by the same pancreatic cells that make insulin, so people with type 1 diabetes lack it too. Pramlintide replaces it at meals, slowing digestion and blunting the sugar spike after eating. Added to insulin, it lowered HbA1c by roughly 0.6-0.7 points in trials lasting up to a year and tended to cause **slight weight loss** rather than gain.[^1][^2] The trade-off is a boxed warning for **severe low blood sugar**, especially in type 1 diabetes, so mealtime insulin is cut by half when it starts.[^3] Today it is mostly a niche option; newer amylin drugs are being developed mainly for obesity.
glance: Approved 2005; boxed warning for severe hypoglycemia
Adults using mealtime insulin whose blood sugar is still not at target
Pen injection under the skin right before each major meal, separate from insulin
Year-long randomized trials in type 1 and type 2 diabetes

blocks.text: Amylin is co-released with insulin from beta cells after meals. Human amylin clumps easily, which makes it unusable as a drug, so pramlintide swaps in three prolines borrowed from rat amylin to keep it soluble while preserving its action.

items: **Stomach:** slows emptying, so glucose enters the blood more gradually
**Liver:** suppresses the glucagon surge after meals, so less sugar is released
**Brain:** increases fullness, which helps explain the small weight loss seen in trials

blocks.text: SymlinPen is approved for adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin but have not reached their glucose targets despite optimized insulin.[^3] The label advises against it for people with an HbA1c above 9%, frequent severe lows, poor adherence to insulin and glucose monitoring, or who take drugs that speed up the gut. It is not approved for children.

rows: HbA1c fell 0.67 points by week 13 vs 0.16 on placebo, with lasting benefit and slight weight loss[^1]
HbA1c fell about 0.6 points; weight -1.4 kg vs +0.7 kg on placebo[^2]
Similar HbA1c drop to placebo, but smaller post-meal spikes, 28% less insulin and weight loss[^4]

blocks.text: It is injected under the skin immediately before each major meal (at least 250 calories or 30 g of carbohydrate), never mixed with insulin. In type 1 diabetes it starts at 15 mcg and rises in 15 mcg steps to 30 or 60 mcg; in type 2 diabetes it starts at 60 mcg and rises to 120 mcg. Steps are at least three days apart to limit nausea, and mealtime insulin is reduced by 50% at the start.[^3]

items: **Boxed warning:** severe hypoglycemia with insulin, most often within three hours of a dose and especially in type 1 diabetes
**Common:** nausea, vomiting, poor appetite and headache, usually easing over the first weeks
**Do not use** with gastroparesis, hypoglycemia unawareness or a serious allergy to the drug[^3]
**Absorption:** slowed digestion can delay oral drugs that need to act fast, such as pain relievers

blocks.text: In the intensive-insulin type 1 trial, nausea affected 63% of people on pramlintide versus 36% on placebo, and severe hypoglycemia was more frequent in those who stayed at 30 mcg.[^4]

evidence.label: Approved; modest glucose benefit with real risks
evidence.text: Randomized trials lasting up to a year show modest HbA1c reductions and small weight loss when pramlintide is added to insulin.[^1][^2] Benefits must be weighed against nausea, extra injections at each main meal and the risk of severe lows.[^3]

faq.q: Is pramlintide a type of insulin?
faq.a: No. It mimics amylin, a separate hormone, and is always used alongside mealtime insulin, never instead of it or mixed with it.

faq.q: Why must mealtime insulin be cut when starting?
faq.a: Pramlintide slows how quickly food raises blood sugar. Without lowering insulin, the insulin can act before the glucose arrives and cause a dangerous low.[^3]
Usually a little. Trials found weight loss of around 1-1.5 kg, compared with slight gain on placebo, but it is not approved for weight management.[^2]

faq.q: How does it relate to newer amylin drugs?
faq.a: Long-acting amylin analogs such as [cagrilintide](/peptides/cagrilintide) and [petrelintide](/peptides/petrelintide) build on the same hormone and are being studied mainly for obesity.
